rv.q: Harrison throws just about everything at this gloriously over-the-top show.

A terrific ensemble performs song-and-dance numbers, there’s great comedy from ventriloquist Paul ­Zerdin, plus a (rather shoehorned-in) 3-D sequence. And Nigel Havers as Friar Tuck on the receiving end of Mr Clary’s waspish gags.
But otherwise, Michael Harrison’s production is an effective celebration of the showy elements of panto that mark most people’s introduction to theatre.
All the same, something feels rotten at the heart of Clary’s panto.
I wholeheartedly confess that Robin Hood has made a merry man out of me.
The Palladium panto should be a genre in its own right.

cn.t: Julian Clary leads a spectacular, extravagant Palladium panto that delivers eye-popping sets and relentless smutty humor, though critics split on whether the formula still charms or feels hollow beneath the glitz.
